Stopnica New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Stopnica, Poland

Not demolished. Despite this record's 'not demolished' classification, its own narrative overwhelmingly describes a destroyed site — one more contradiction worth flagging rather than resolving. During the ghetto's liquidation in November 1942, around 400 people, mostly the elderly and children, were shot here and buried on the spot; their remains were reportedly exhumed and burned in 1944. Afterward, the site was formally closed by municipal decree in 1964 and 1970, farmed and grazed, and partly built over with a transformer station in the early 1970s. It served a community that, at its 1921 peak, made up over three-quarters of Stopnica's population — a town that once hosted sessions of the Council (Sejm) of Four Lands, the central Jewish self-governing body of the old Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
